summary: Douglas County, Oregon, Umpqua NF lookout: early-1920s platform, 14-foot tower in 1930, removed in the 1960s or 1970s. No source describes the site today.

events.note: Crow's nest platform and Adirondack shelter in the early 1920s (register). Forest Lookouts dates a five-post, 12-foot platform to c.1922.
Harold Church named as a lookout stationed at Twin Lakes
14-foot tower (register, firelookout.com). Forest Lookouts' July 1930 item describes a new tower of poles cut on the ground.
Forest Lookouts lists a 15-foot tower with a gable-roofed cab, about 1938. No source says whether it replaced the 1930 tower.
Lookout crew at the station, per a July 1938 supply flight item
Register and firelookout.com say removed or destroyed in the 1970s. The year 1970 stands for the decade only.

evidence.supports: crow's nest platform and Adirondack shelter in the early 1920s
evidence.quote: A crude crow's nest platform and an Adirondack shelter were set up here in the early 1920's.

evidence.supports: five wood posts with a 12-foot platform, around 1922
evidence.quote: c.1922: The lookout consisted of five wood posts supporting a 12-foot high lookout tree platform.
They were replaced with a 14' live-in tower in 1930.

evidence.supports: 14-foot L-4 tower replaced the early set-up in 1930
evidence.quote: a 14' wooden L-4 tower replaced it in 1930.

evidence.supports: July 1930 new tower of poles cut on the ground
evidence.quote: A new tower, constructed of poles cut on the ground, has been erected on Twin Lakes mountain.
c.1938: A 15-foot lookout tower with a gable roofed cab constructed.

evidence.supports: Harold Church stationed at Twin Lakes in 1927
evidence.quote: Harold Church, a brother of Dr. H.C. Church, a lookout stationed at Twin Lakes

evidence.supports: July 1938 supply flight, crew at the station
evidence.quote: The plane skimmed low enough over the station to see the faces of the lookout crew awaiting arrival of their bedding and grub.
The tower was removed in the 1970s.

corrections.why: 3.7 m (12 ft) matches the c.1922 five-post platform, not the 1930 tower. The register and firelookout.com give the 1930 tower as 14 feet (about 4.3 m). Forest Lookouts' 15-foot figure for c.1938 would be about 4.6 m, so the sources disagree; 4.3 m follows the two sources that describe the 1930 tower.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The early set-up is described as a crow's nest platform with an Adirondack shelter (register) and as a five-post, 12-foot platform about 1922 (Forest Lookouts). Both describe a pre-1930 structure, so both are kept in the events.

notes_for_editor: Removal year disputed: 1962 (Forest Lookouts) vs the 1970s (register, firelookout.com). The c.1938 15-foot tower with gable cab (Forest Lookouts) does not match the 14-foot 1930 tower; it may be a rebuild but no source says so. Correction proposed for height_m (3.7 to 4.3) because 3.7 m is the 12-foot early platform. Access and current site condition are not described by any source, so no access or visit fact is written. An unsourced social media post saying the lookout was removed in the 1930s was not used.
